messages:
oncall-bot: Paging oncall (severity=P1) — serving cluster 'us-east-1a' reports multiple GPU container crashes and node disconnects. Symptoms: repeated CUDA_DRIVER_TIMEOUT, OOMs in runtime, and IB retransmit counters rising. Please ack and join #incidents asap. https://grafana.internal/alerts/3301123344

maya: acked. I'm on it. Jumping into logs now.

leo: seeing the same from runtime. k8s shows 4 pods in CrashLoopBackOff across two nodes. dmesg on node-34 contains repeated 'mlx5: QP error' and 'ib event: link down' entries.

jordan: on the serving side, KV-cache replicas are getting split — requests timing out then piling up, causing burst allocation and CUDA OOMs. Rolling back to smaller batch size didn't help immediately.

maya: quick customer impact check — traffic dropped ~35% for prod-route /v1/generate, latency 95p spiked to 8s then errors. tagging SLO risk. @customer-ops please prepare comms if we need to notify impacted customers.

customer-ops: acknowledged, prepping template. Holding until we confirm blast radius.

ops-bot: deploys blocked: recent infra kernel patch rolled out to rack 7 three hours ago. Change-ID: CHG-8891.

elaine: can someone run `ibstat` and `ibdump` on node-34 and node-35? Need counters.

leo: pasted output snippet:
```
# ibstat -p
Port 1: LinkDown
Port 2: Active
# cat /sys/class/infiniband/mlx5_0/ports/1/counters/retransmitted
retransmitted: 123987
# dmesg | tail -n 10
[ 12345.678901] mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0: CQ error (EQ 6) QP 1280 vendor synd 0x1
[ 12345.679012] NMI watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3
```

maya: retransmit numbers are huge, suggests link flapping or microburst-induced drops. Probable packet loss causing RPC stalls and KV cache thrash -> OOMs due to retry amplification.

jordan: mitigation plan: 1) cordon node-34, migrate serving pods to warmed nodes in same AZ with fallback model variant; 2) reduce batch size and disable autoscale temporarily; 3) apply per-pod env var to force smaller KV working set. Who can do the cordon/migrate?

leo: I'll cordon and drain node-34, then scale up fallback pool by +3. Command: `kubectl cordon node-34 && kubectl drain node-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

maya: while that's happening, runtime team: drop gdr/HPC offload for affected pods to force GPUDirect fallback? That should reduce IB traffic. Add env `REDWOOD_USE_GDR=false` and restart pods.

jordan: good idea. Runtime restart sequence (do one pod at a time):
```
kubectl set env deploy/serve-prod REDWOOD_USE_GDR=false --namespace=prod
kubectl rollout restart deploy/serve-prod --namespace=prod --field-selector=status.phase=Running
```

leo: draining now. moving two pods to fallback nodes. scaling fallback pool.

(10m later)

leo: node-34 drain succeeded, pods rescheduled. retransmit counters on node-35 still climbing though.

elaine: we should also throttle IB probe/multipath to avoid triggering hardware QP resets — lowering mlx5 interrupt moderation and enabling ECN marking for that rack. I'll coordinate with infra.

maya: customer-ops: impact is moderate; errors at 5-8% for top customers. Recommend holding public comms but notify 3 customers on the edge.

customer-ops: notified 3 accounts with brief note and we shared temporary mitigation ETA ~30m.

ops-bot: CHG-8891 (kernel patch) suspects: rollback recommended if infra changes correlate. Any evidence?

leo: kernel patch timeline aligns with first alerts. We have logs of link resets post-patch on multiple hosts. I've flagged infra-rollback as option.

jordan: If rollback is risky, alternative is to route traffic away from affected rack and keep GDR disabled. Which is less intrusive?

maya: routing away is less risky short-term. I'm switching route policy to prefer us-east-1b/c and adding capacity there. Executing policy change.

(5m)

maya: policy change applied. Request distribution shifted ~70% to healthy AZs. Error rate dropped to ~1.4% and latency 95p down to 400ms. Good signal.

leo: GPU OOMs stopped after GDR disabled and reschedule; crash loops not returning. I still see higher retransmits but less customer impact.

elaine: infra will open rollback window for CHG-8891 in 30m if we want to try a controlled rollback to verify causality. Recommend we keep rack isolated until then.

maya: agree. We're keeping the incident open and moving to mitigation->monitoring. I will handoff to night oncall in 50m.

jordan: follow-up action items to capture: 1) postmortem with packet captures and dmesg timeline; 2) add guardrail to disable GDR automatically if IB retransmit threshold crossed; 3) investigate kernel change relation; 4) improve autoscaler backpressure logic to avoid OOM cascade.

customer-ops: preparing customer update noting partial traffic reroute and mitigation.

(handoff)

maya: handing off to @leo for night watch. Current state: traffic routed away, GDR disabled on affected pool, node-34 cordoned, fallback capacity up. Monitoring for retransmit drops; if retransmit > 200k in next 30m, escalate to infra rollback.

leo: acked. I'll monitor graphs and packet counters and will page immediately if we see regression. Leaving a note in the incident tracker: https://incidents.internal/3301123344

oncall-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged by leo. Next rotation: night-oncall.

maya: thanks team. Will write timeline + initial blameless postmortem draft.

jordan: tagging for postmortem: eng-runtime, eng-infra, eng-sre, customer-success.

elaine: infra will schedule rollback window and collect binary package logs.

leo: closing thread for now — will reopen if retransmits spike or pods crash again.
